name: Jean Nouvel
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Nouvel opened his first practice at age 25 (1970) and obtained his degree in 1971, but his first independently verifiable notable achievement — winning the PAN architecture competition — came in 1972 at age 27, and his first major building (Institut du Monde Arabe) was completed in 1987 at age 42.
early_history_summary: Nouvel studied at the École des Beaux-Arts in Paris, winning first prize in the national entrance competition in 1966. From 1967 to 1970 he was assistant to architects Claude Parent and Paul Virilio, who made him a project manager after one year. He started his own practice with François Seigneur in 1970 but did not achieve notable recognition until the PAN competition in 1972.
family_context_summary: Son of Renée and Roger Nouvel, who were teachers; his father became county chief school superintendent. Parents encouraged mathematics and languages but compromised on architecture as a safer career than art.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were educators; no direct architectural or artistic domain transfer documented.
evidence_summary: Nouvel's early career involved assistant work under Claude Parent and Paul Virilio from 1967-1970 and starting his own practice at 25, but his first notable competition win (PAN, 1972) and first major building (Institut du Monde Arabe, 1981-1987) both came after age 26. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Gilbert Bécaud
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Bécaud was a working songwriter from 1948 and was accepted by Sacem at 20, but his first public performance came in 1954 at age 27 and his first hit ('La Corrida') in 1956 at age 29. No material, independently verifiable public milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Bécaud learned piano at a young age and attended the Conservatoire de Nice. He joined the French Resistance in 1942, began songwriting in 1948, and wrote for Marie Bizet as part of a trio. He toured as a pianist with Jacques Pills and met Édith Piaf, who suggested he start singing in 1953, but his first performance and hits came after age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Toulon, France; learned piano at a young age and attended the Conservatoire de Nice. Left school in 1942 to join the French Resistance.
evidence_summary: Bécaud was professionally active as a songwriter from 1948 and composed for artists including Édith Piaf, but his own performing career began in 1953-1954 (ages 26-27) with no documented hit records or major public performances by age 26. His breakthrough as 'Monsieur 100,000 Volts' came in the mid-to-late 1950s.

name: Bettina Heinen-Ayech
milestone_by_age_26: In 1955 at age 18, her paintings were included by Frankfurt gallerist Hanna Bekker vom Rath in the major touring exhibition 'Deutsche Kunst der Gegenwart' (1955/56), shown alongside works by Paul Klee, Max Beckmann, Max Ernst, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, and Käthe Kollwitz on a tour of South America, Africa, and Asia.
early_history_summary: Heinen-Ayech received her first artistic training from family friend and painter Erwin Bowien, who remained her mentor. She attended the Cologne Werkschulen from 1954, and at age 18 her watercolors and drawings were exhibited for the first time in Bad Homburg and then included in a major international touring exhibition alongside some of the most renowned German artists of the era. She later studied at the Munich Art Academy and the Royal Danish Academy of Art in Copenhagen.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Johann Jakob Josef 'Hanns' Heinen, a journalist and editor-in-chief of the Solinger Tageblatt, and Erna Steinhoff-Heinen. The family home was characterized by art and openness, and family friend Erwin Bowien (a painter) was her mentor from an early age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a journalist, editor-in-chief, and playwright; family friend Erwin Bowien was a painter who served as her dedicated mentor from early youth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dedicated mentor, family art environment, early exhibition access, Cologne Werkschulen
evidence_summary: Heinen-Ayech benefited from a culturally rich family environment (father a journalist/playwright) and sustained mentorship from painter Erwin Bowien from a young age. At 18, her work was selected by Frankfurt gallerist Hanna Bekker vom Rath for a major international touring exhibition alongside Klee, Beckmann, and Ernst — a remarkable early milestone. She subsequently trained at three art academies (Cologne, Munich, Copenhagen) and received cultural ministry grants in 1959 and 1962.

name: Andy Cole
milestone_by_age_26: In the 1993-94 season at age 22-23, Cole was the Premier League top scorer with 34 league goals (41 in all competitions) for Newcastle United, won the PFA Young Player of the Year award, and set a club record for goals in a season that still stands.
early_history_summary: Cole came through the youth ranks at Arsenal but made only one appearance before loan spells at Fulham and Bristol City. He joined Newcastle United in 1993 for a club-record fee and immediately became a prolific striker, scoring 41 goals in his first full season and forming a devastating partnership with Peter Beardsley. He moved to Manchester United in 1995 and won the Premier League in 1995-96.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Arsenal academy, Premier League era, Beardsley partnership, Kevin Keegan
evidence_summary: Cole's early career was built on the Arsenal youth academy pipeline and the explosive growth of the Premier League era. His record-breaking 41-goal season at Newcastle in 1993-94, aided by Kevin Keegan's management and Peter Beardsley's partnership, made him one of the most feared strikers in English football by age 23. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Ágnes Keleti
milestone_by_age_26: By age 16 (1937) she was Hungarian National Champion in gymnastics, and at age 26 (1947) she won the Central European Gymnastics Championships, having won ten national championship titles between 1937 and 1956.
early_history_summary: Keleti began gymnastics training at age 4 at Budapest's Jewish VAC Club and became Hungarian National Champion at 16. Her career was interrupted by WWII; she survived the Holocaust using false identity papers, worked as a maid, and lost her father at Auschwitz. After the war, she resumed training, won the Hungarian championship in 1946, and dominated the Central European Gymnastics Championships in 1947. She later won five Olympic gold medals at the 1952 and 1956 Games.
family_context_summary: Born in Budapest to a Jewish family. Father was murdered at Auschwitz during WWII; mother and sister survived using Swiss/Swedish protection papers. She survived by purchasing false identity papers and working as a maid in a small village.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Family was Jewish and suffered severely during the Holocaust.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early training at VAC Club, national champion at 16, Holocaust survival, post-war comeback
evidence_summary: Keleti's extraordinary early gymnastics talent was evident from age 4, leading to a national championship at 16. Her career was brutally interrupted by the Holocaust — she survived using false papers, lost her father at Auschwitz, and collected bodies during the Siege of Budapest. After the war, she returned to win the Central European Championships at 26 and later became one of the most decorated Olympic gymnasts ever with five gold medals. Her story is one of extreme adversity catalyzing rather than destroying determination.

name: Glenn Hughes
milestone_by_age_26: By age 22 (1973), Hughes joined Deep Purple — then one of the world's biggest rock bands — as bassist and co-lead vocalist, and by age 26 (1977) he had recorded three albums with them including the classic 'Burn' (1974), 'Stormbringer' (1974), and 'Come Taste the Band' (1975).
early_history_summary: Hughes fronted the Midlands beat combo Finders Keepers in the 1960s as a teenager, then formed the acclaimed funk-rock band Trapeze in 1969 at age 18. He recorded three albums with Trapeze (1970-1972) before being recruited by Deep Purple in 1973 after members Ritchie Blackmore, Jon Lord, and Ian Paice scouted him at the Whisky a Go Go. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of Deep Purple in 2016.
family_context_summary: Born in Cannock, Staffordshire, England. Not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early band formation, British rock ecosystem, exceptional vocal/bass talent, Deep Purple recruitment
evidence_summary: Hughes built his career through early and sustained musical practice from his teens in the British Midlands rock scene. His exceptional funk-inspired bass playing and soulful countertenor vocal range set him apart, leading from Finders Keepers to Trapeze (three albums by age 21) and then to Deep Purple at 22. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources; his rise appears largely self-created through domain repetition and talent.

name: Kaká
milestone_by_age_26: At age 20 (2002), Kaká won the FIFA World Cup with Brazil. At age 25 (2007), he won the UEFA Champions League with AC Milan as the tournament's top scorer, and won the Ballon d'Or and FIFA World Player of the Year — the highest individual honors in football.
early_history_summary: Kaká began at São Paulo FC's youth academy at age 8, signed a contract at 15, and made his senior debut at 18 in 2001, leading São Paulo to the Torneio Rio-São Paulo championship. He joined AC Milan in 2003 for €8.5 million, immediately becoming a starter and winning Serie A in his first season. He was named Serie A Footballer of the Year in 2004 and went on to win the 2006-07 Champions League as top scorer, earning the 2007 Ballon d'Or.
primary_leverage_engine: Football talent and early professional debut
family_context_summary: Born to Simone dos Santos, an elementary school teacher, and Bosco Izecson Pereira Leite, a civil engineer. The family was financially secure, allowing Kaká to focus on school and football. His younger brother Digão and cousin Eduardo Delani are also professional footballers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were a teacher and a civil engineer; not directly in football, but the family was financially secure and supportive of football training from a young age. Brother and cousin also became professional footballers.
primary_early_advantage_tags: São Paulo FC academy, financially secure family, Brazilian football culture, early professional debut, World Cup at 20
evidence_summary: Kaká's path was enabled by a financially secure family that allowed focus on football, access to São Paulo FC's elite youth academy from age 8, and immersion in Brazil's football culture. His exceptional talent was evident early — he signed at 15, debuted professionally at 18, and was a World Cup winner at 20. A career-threatening spinal fracture at 18 tested his resolve but he recovered fully. By 25, he was the best player in the world.

name: J. K. Rowling
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Rowling conceived the idea for Harry Potter in 1990 at age 25, but the first book was not published until 1997 when she was 32. By age 26 (1991), she had no published novels and was working as a researcher at Amnesty International before moving to Portugal to teach English.
early_history_summary: Rowling studied French and Classics at the University of Exeter, then worked in London including as a researcher at Amnesty International. She conceived the Harry Potter idea on a train in 1990, moved to Portugal to teach English in 1991, and returned to Edinburgh in 1993. The first Harry Potter book was published in 1997 after years of writing in longhand.
family_context_summary: Father was an aircraft engineer at Rolls Royce; mother was a science technician. Mother was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis when Rowling was a teenager and died in 1990.
evidence_summary: Rowling wrote from a young age (her first book at age six, a novel at eleven) but had no published work by age 26. She worked at Amnesty International and as a teacher before Harry Potter was published in 1997 at age 32. Her extraordinary success arrived well after age 26.

name: Georges Charpak
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Charpak graduated from École des Mines in 1948 (age 24) and became a CNRS researcher in 1948-1949, but his PhD in nuclear physics was completed in 1954 (age 30), his CERN career began in 1959 (age 35), and his Nobel Prize-winning work on the multiwire proportional chamber came in 1968 (age 44). No material scientific milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: Charpak moved from Poland to Paris at age 7. During WWII he served in the French Resistance and was deported to Dachau concentration camp in 1944. After the war, he became a French citizen, graduated from École des Mines in 1948, and became a research student under Frédéric Joliot-Curie at the Collège de France in 1949, securing a CNRS position. His PhD came in 1954 and his Nobel Prize in 1992.
family_context_summary: Born to Jewish parents in Poland; family moved to Paris when he was 7. Survived Dachau concentration camp during WWII.
evidence_summary: Charpak's early career was disrupted by WWII (resistance, Dachau). By age 26 (1950), he was a beginning CNRS researcher under Joliot-Curie but had not yet completed his PhD or produced notable scientific work. His material achievements — PhD (1954), CERN career (1959), wire chamber invention (1968), Nobel Prize (1992) — all came well after age 26.

name: Václav Havel
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Havel worked as a stagehand and dramaturge at Prague's Theatre on the Balustrade from 1960, but his first full-length play 'The Garden Party' did not premiere until December 3, 1963, when he was 27 — just past the age 26 cutoff.
early_history_summary: Havel was born into a wealthy Prague family (grandfather was a real estate developer, father built Barrandov Terraces). Due to his bourgeois background, he was barred from humanities programs and did an apprenticeship as a chemical laboratory assistant. He worked as a stagehand at ABC Theatre from 1959, then at the Theatre on the Balustrade from 1960, becoming dramaturge in 1962. His first play premiered in December 1963.
family_context_summary: Born into a wealthy Prague family celebrated for entrepreneurial and cultural accomplishments. Grandfather built a landmark entertainment complex on Wenceslas Square; father was a real estate developer behind Barrandov Terraces; uncle built one of Europe's largest film studios. Mother came from an influential family; her father was a Czechoslovak ambassador and journalist.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was in real estate development and cultural entrepreneurship; not directly in theatre or literature, but provided a strong intellectual and cultural environment.
evidence_summary: Havel came from a wealthy, culturally prominent Prague family but was barred from higher education in humanities due to his bourgeois class background under communism. He worked as a stagehand and dramaturge at the Theatre on the Balustrade from 1960, but his first play 'The Garden Party' premiered on December 3, 1963, when he was 27 — narrowly missing the age 26 cutoff.

name: Omar Sharif
milestone_by_age_26: From his film debut in 1954 at age 22 in 'The Blazing Sun' (which screened at Cannes) through 1958 (age 26), Sharif appeared in approximately 24 Egyptian films and became one of Egypt's biggest movie stars and matinee idols, later achieving global fame with 'Lawrence of Arabia' (1962).
early_history_summary: Born Michel Chalhoub in Alexandria to a wealthy Melkite Greek Catholic family, Sharif attended the exclusive Victoria College and graduated from Cairo University with a degree in mathematics and physics. He worked in his father's precious wood business before director Youssef Chahine discovered him and cast him in 'The Blazing Sun' (1954). He quickly rose to stardom, converted to Islam in 1955 to marry actress Faten Hamama, and became Egypt's most popular romantic leading man.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy family; father Yusef Chalhoub was a precious woods merchant who moved from Zahlé to Alexandria. Mother Claire Saada was a noted society hostess whose house was visited by King Farouk. He attended the exclusive Victoria College in Alexandria.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family was in the precious woods merchant business; not in entertainment. However, the family's wealth and society connections provided access to exclusive education and social networks.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, society connections, Victoria College, Egyptian cinema golden age, Chahine discovery, Faten Hamama partnership
evidence_summary: Sharif's rise to stardom was facilitated by his wealthy family background (father a precious woods merchant, mother a society hostess visited by King Farouk), exclusive education at Victoria College, and the golden age of Egyptian cinema. Director Youssef Chahine, a school friend, discovered him and cast him in his debut film at 22. His marriage to leading actress Faten Hamama cemented his status as Egypt's most popular romantic screen star. By 26, he had appeared in approximately 24 films — a remarkable level of productivity and recognition.

name: Javier Solana
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: By age 26 (1968), Solana was a Fulbright scholar and teaching assistant at the University of Virginia working toward his physics PhD, which he completed in 1971 at age 29. His material achievements — professorship, parliamentary election, NATO Secretary General — all came well after age 26.
early_history_summary: Solana came from a prominent Spanish intellectual family. He studied at Complutense University, was expelled in 1963 for student activism against Franco, joined the PSOE clandestinely in 1964, and won a Fulbright Scholarship in 1965 to study in the US. He was a teaching assistant at the University of Virginia while pursuing his doctorate in physics, which he received in 1971. He returned to Spain to teach physics before entering politics.
family_context_summary: Born to a prominent Spanish family; father was a chemistry professor who died when Javier was 19. Great-uncle Salvador de Madariaga was a diplomat, writer, and historian. Elder brother Luis was imprisoned for political activities against Franco.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a chemistry professor; family was politically active and intellectually distinguished. Great-uncle was a diplomat and European integration advocate.
evidence_summary: Solana came from a prominent intellectual family (father a chemistry professor, great-uncle a diplomat). By 26, he was a Fulbright scholar and teaching assistant at the University of Virginia pursuing his PhD, which he completed in 1971 at 29. His material career achievements — professorship at Complutense, parliamentary election (1977), NATO Secretary General (1995) — all came after age 26.
